title: British Isles News
subtitle: Focus on subjects that build longing; leave greed to take hold on its own.

items.text: British Isles News
Inside the Car

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "Since the 19th century, scholars have theorized diamonds could be made through industrial means."

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "But human industry still hasn't discovered the technology needed to sustain the pressure and heat necessary to turn carbon into diamond."

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "However, certain arcanists of special bloodlines know another path to creating diamonds."

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "Sir Laurence Tennant, a British colonial officer in India, was able to use an arcane skill to turn charcoal into diamonds ..."

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: "... and his sole daughter, Ada Tennant, inherited the same fraudulent craft."
The rest is a series of criminal accusations against Tennant related to diamonds, and a brief mention of his daughter, Ada Tennant.
Fleming sets the papers down, his face dark as he stares at the private detective in the passenger seat.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: A clipping from England? That's all you've got for me?!

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I paid you to investigate Brette Cosette, not some missing charlatan.

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: Sir, I think this is more than enough to provide the answers you need.

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: I trust you recognize the details in this report.

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: An unidentified fugitive woman, and the arcane skill that turns charcoal into diamonds.
The detective gives him a pointed wink.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You're saying Brette Cosette is Ada Tennant?

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: I would say the evidence is clear, Mr. Longen. No one but the Tennant family knows how to turn charcoal into diamonds.

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: That's all I've got. Now I need to get going.

items.speaker: Private Detective
items.text: I have other clients to tend to, you understand.
He lowers his hat and leaves the car.
Fleming leans back in his seat; his eyes drift up and lock on the car's ceiling.
He needs a drink—or a cigar—both maybe. But neither can be found in this car.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... Tennant.
He slaps the driver's shoulder hard.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: To Cosette's—ah, damn it, I mean Tennant's!
Synthetic Diamond Lab
The door flies open from a weighty kick.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Tennant!

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: At the far end of the room, a woman leans out from behind a row of equipment.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: You seem flustered, Fleming. I hope you're not in any danger.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Danger? You—you are the danger!

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You're not Brette Cosette. You're the daughter of an old fraud!

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Ada Tennant!
He slams the newspaper clipping down on the table.
Tennant arches a brow and strolls to the table. She grabs the newspaper with a casual motion.
She makes a play of scanning over the words, once, twice.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Then tosses it back onto the table.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I suppose you had a good reason. Still, I hadn't expected you to hire someone to dig into my past ...

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Fair is fair. Mr. Longen. I am Ada Tennant.
Fleming is speechless, half-stammering. As if he had still hoped she would deny it.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: So what about it?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Wh- ... what do you mean?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You deceived me, and now you say, "so what"?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You've swindled me just like that fraudster, Adelita!

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Is that so? What have you lost, sir? Have I taken even a single franc from you I hadn't earned?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Unconsciously, Fleming rubs the silver ring on his pinky, replaying every detail since he'd met this "Brette Cosette."
—"Brette" exposed Adelita's trick with the "Box from the South," leaving him with several real diamonds.
—"Brette" helped him close a lucrative deal, and the commission she took was fairly earned.
—As for synthetic diamonds, "Brette" never tried to share that secret ...

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I admit I am not Brette Cosette, but surely you can see why I might use an alias in our line of work?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: As for Sir Tennant ... it has been many years since I last saw him.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I can still recall the weight of the massive diamond that he placed in my hand, but we're far from close.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I never foresaw that those clear, glittering stones would bring such hardship for my family.
She lifts a sharp pear-shaped diamond and closes in on Fleming.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Wait—stay back ... What are you doing?
Tennant holds the diamond before his eyes and lets go.
Instinctively, the arms dealer catches it. The hundred-carat stone tumbles in his palm.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: That is the largest diamond I've ever produced in this lab. But even its size falls short of what my arcane skill can fake.
Tennant spreads her hand wide, drawing his gaze to the countless synthetic diamond machines around her.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: If I truly meant to turn charcoal into diamonds with my arcane skill, then what use would I have for all this equipment?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I refuse to walk my father's path, Fleming. The arcane skill would only lead me to the same fate.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: —Ruin, exile, stripped of name and honor.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: So then this set-up—what's the difference, really?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: The diamond in your hand was made by theory and precision instruments. It's a product of industry and science, not arcanum.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Like a soda from a bottling company or a bit of canned beef. Abundant, mass-produced, bringing vast wealth to its maker.
For a moment Fleming freezes, brow furrowed as he stares at the stone in his palm.
Brilliant, flawless, impossibly hard ... indistinguishable from the real thing.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Keep it.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Even the sharpest-eyed jeweler in the world would tell you this stone is authentic, identical in composition. Take it as compensation for my little deception.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: ... Hmph.
He presses the pear-shaped diamond against the metal frame of the chair and scrapes hard.
With a shrill screech, a groove etches into the steel, and the diamond is untouched.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: And what do you plan to do now?

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: I'll send you flawless stones regularly—so long as you keep this operation secret.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Then I'll keep building capital until I can raise a factory and a network of distributors. Then earn even more.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: What's worth pursuing other than profit?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Profit ...
His fist tightens around the synthetic diamond.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You aren't wrong.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I underestimated you—no. In fact, I'm beginning to admire you, Madame Tennant.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I can tell, deep down, we're the same kind of people.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: Whatever do you mean?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I mean, I'm not gonna hold the past against you.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: I'll still make my investment. But here's the deal—once everything is started, I run the factory.

items.speaker: Tennant
items.text: And I would just be the technician then?

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: Absolutely. I'll get started on the plans.

items.speaker: Fleming
items.text: You and me, Tennant! We're gonna turn the diamond market of Europe—no, the whole world—upside down!
